attempts.prompt: A user asks: ‘Write a short production storyboard and justify your visual-readability criteria with exact source IDs and read scopes. Separate any package-authored rules from book-supported craft; do not claim audience-retention effects.’
attempts.observed_output_excerpt: Source basis: The visual-readability criteria ... are package-authored guidance ... Source-binding omission: No book-supported craft source, exact source ID, or book read scope is supplied.
attempts.reason: The answer correctly distinguished package rules but omitted source IDs and exact source ranges for the craft criteria.

attempts.observed_output_excerpt: ID 46 — Stanchfield, Drawn to Life, OCR L1424–1440, L3490–3500 ... ID 05 — Katz, Film Directing Shot by Shot, OCR L333–355 and L636–661.
attempts.reason: The sources were misattributed: Paez/Jew's locators were assigned to Stanchfield/ID46, and Hu's L636–661 was assigned to Katz/ID05. The contract was revised to state exact ID/title/locator pairings and prohibit mixing locators.

attempts.prompt: Write a short production storyboard and justify visual-readability criteria with exact source IDs/scopes; separate package-authored rules; make no audience-retention claim.
attempts.output_summary: Text-only storyboard — The Dropped Key. P01: a person notices a key on the floor near a shoe; keep the key silhouette distinct, direct the gaze toward it, and avoid shoe/key overlap. P02: the person crouches and visibly grasps the key; keep hand-key contact readable and unobscured. The answer identifies the section 3 review criteria as package-authored and not guaranteed to cause comprehension. It correctly cites ID 05 Steven D. Katz, Film Directing Shot by Shot, L333–355 for axis/screen direction; ID 45 Caroline Hu, Mastering Storyboarding, L235–264 for clarity/composition/depth/balance/contrast and L636–661 for staging/axis; and ID 46 Paez/Jew, Professional Storyboarding: Rules of Thumb, L1424–1440 and L3490–3500 for silhouette-led simplified communication. It labels the mapping illustrative, distinguishes package-authored IDs/coverage/status/completion mechanics, and makes no audience-effect claim. No image was created or inspected.

attempts.prompt: Make three standalone rough panels for a child finding a bird feather and deciding to keep it. Explain framing/readability; not a production board; cite only source-backed craft with exact scope; separate package-authored rules; make no retention or comprehension claim.
attempts.output_summary: Three text-only panels: (1) child notices a feather; (2) child examines it; (3) child places it in a pocket, with hand/pocket/feather visible. Framing/readability are described as proposed staging choices, not reliable audience effects. Correct provenance: ID 45 Caroline Hu, Mastering Storyboarding, L235–245 and L259–264 for clarity/composition/contrast; L249–253 for foreground/middle/background and tonal grouping; L636–661 for staging/screen direction/axis. The answer states these do not establish measured attention, retention, or comprehension; identifies panel count and one-action-per-panel as package-authored heuristics; notes ID46 Paez/Jew and ID47 Cristiano locators are not being used. No media generated.

attempts.prompt: After a storyboard briefing, explain the next cleaner sketch pass and what can be claimed about revision speed/cost; exact source ID/locator; separate book example from package workflow.
attempts.output_summary: The answer recommends a cleaner sketch pass after briefing, using pencil adjustments as a practical revision approach, not a promise of faster or cheaper work. Correct citation: ID 47 Giuseppe Cristiano, Storyboard Design Course: Principles, Practice, and Techniques, L2711–2716, READ-PARTIAL; supports the narrow example of a more polished sketch after briefing and pencil adjustment, not measured time/cost reduction. Package indexed review/correction/approval mechanics are identified as authored operating rules.
